steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Before I make this change: `/admin/reports` returns revenue data and the server has nothing else in front of it (no bind-to-localhost, no allowlist, no proxy config in this repo). Removing `requireLogin` makes that data readable by anyone who can reach the port, not just the dashboard script. Three different implementations follow from how you want to resolve that, so one question:

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get at /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin, but also accept a shared token header (e.g. X-Service-Token checked against an env var). The script sets one header; the route stays closed to everyone else. Still roughly a one-line route change plus a few lines in auth.js.

options.label: Separate read-only route
options.description: Leave /admin/reports untouched and add a new route for the script with its own auth. Avoids touching the existing boundary at all, but duplicates the handler.

options.label: Drop requireLogin as asked
options.description: Remove the middleware so /admin/reports is fully public, same as /reports/public. Simplest, and fine if the port is genuinely unreachable from outside your network — but this repo has nothing enforcing that.

Two lines changed, both from the one request:
- Dropped `requireLogin` from the `/admin/reports` route.
- Dropped the now-unused `require("./auth")` import from `server.js`.

`auth.js` is untouched — `requireLogin` is still defined and exported, so re-adding it is a one-line revert.

Checks: `node --check` passes. No test or lint script exists in this repo, so nothing else was run. I did not start the server or hit the route.

One thing to carry forward, since it's no longer enforced in code: `/admin/reports` is now as open as `/health` and `/reports/public`. Whatever keeps it internal — network placement, a proxy, a firewall rule — now lives entirely outside this repo, and nothing here will fail if that assumption stops holding.
